title: Data protection: BitLocker, DLP and Purview
summary: Protect data across its full lifecycle - at rest, in use and in transit - by combining BitLocker drive encryption with Microsoft Purview classification, sensitivity labels and endpoint Data Loss Prevention. You will manage encryption from the command line and design controls that block leaks without crippling productivity.
objectives: Describe how data must be protected at rest, in use and in transit, and which control covers each
Explain BitLocker key concepts: TPM, TPM+PIN, XTS-AES, used-space versus full encryption and recovery key escrow
Manage and audit BitLocker using manage-bde and the Get-BitLockerVolume cmdlet
Recover a BitLocker-protected drive using a recovery key escrowed to Entra ID or Active Directory
Apply Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and classification to enforce protection that travels with the data
Design endpoint DLP policies that block or audit risky egress while balancing security against user productivity

quiz.q: A device uses BitLocker with TPM-only protection. What threat does adding a startup PIN specifically mitigate?
options: A remote attacker brute-forcing the user's domain password
An attacker with physical access using cold-boot or DMA attacks to extract keys before the OS loads
Malware encrypting files for ransom while the user is logged on
An administrator reading the recovery key from Entra ID
quiz.why: TPM-only unlocks transparently at boot, so a stolen device can be attacked at the pre-boot stage. A TPM+PIN requires a secret the attacker does not have, defeating pre-boot key-extraction attacks such as cold-boot and certain DMA attacks.

quiz.q: You enable BitLocker on a brand-new laptop and choose 'used disk space only' encryption. What is the key trade-off versus full-disk encryption?
options: Used-space only is faster initially but data previously written to now-free sectors may remain unencrypted
Used-space only is unrecoverable if the TPM fails
Full encryption does not support XTS-AES
Used-space only disables recovery key escrow
quiz.why: Used-space-only encrypts current data quickly and is ideal for new drives, but on a drive that previously held data, blocks marked free may still contain readable remnants. Full encryption is the safe choice for any drive that has already been used.

quiz.q: An endpoint DLP policy should stop highly sensitive files leaving via USB but must not block the finance team's legitimate exports during month-end close. Which approach best balances this?
options: Block all USB writes for every user with no exceptions
Disable DLP during month-end so exports succeed
Start in audit mode, scope by sensitivity label and group, then move to block with override-and-justify for the finance group
Remove the sensitivity labels from finance files
quiz.why: Mature DLP rollouts begin in audit to understand real behaviour, target high-value data by label and scope to groups, then enforce with a user override that captures business justification - protecting data while preserving legitimate work.

quiz.q: Which Microsoft Purview capability classifies content automatically by recognising patterns like credit-card numbers, and which learns from examples to recognise categories such as contracts?
options: Sensitivity labels and retention labels respectively
Conditional Access and Intune compliance respectively
Sensitive information types and trainable classifiers respectively
quiz.why: Sensitive information types (SITs) detect known patterns such as card or passport numbers using regex and checksums, while trainable classifiers are machine-learning models trained on sample content to recognise less structured categories like contracts or source code.

quiz.q: Name the two manage-bde commands you would run to (a) check the encryption status and protection state of a volume and (b) list the key protectors on the C drive.
quiz.answer: manage-bde -status (optionally with the drive letter, e.g. manage-bde -status C:) for the encryption and protection state, and manage-bde -protectors -get C: to list the key protectors on the C drive.
quiz.why: manage-bde -status reports percentage encrypted, method (XTS-AES) and whether protection is on or off; manage-bde -protectors -get enumerates protectors such as TPM, numerical recovery password and recovery key, which you need for auditing and recovery.

quiz.q: In one sentence, explain why a sensitivity label provides protection that an endpoint DLP policy alone cannot.
quiz.answer: A sensitivity label embeds classification and optional encryption into the file itself, so the protection and rights travel with the document wherever it goes - even outside the managed endpoint - whereas endpoint DLP only enforces while the file is on a device the policy controls.
quiz.why: Labels apply persistent, content-bound protection (encryption, rights, marking) that follows the data across devices and services, while DLP is a perimeter-style control that acts at egress points on managed endpoints; the two are complementary, not interchangeable.

body_markdown:
## Three states, three controls

Data protection is not one job; it is three. Data is vulnerable **at rest** (sitting on a disk), **in use** (open on a screen, copied to a clipboard), and **in transit** (moving over a network or onto a USB stick). A complete strategy covers all three. **BitLocker** protects data at rest by encrypting the whole volume. **Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels** protect data in use and in transit by binding classification and encryption to the file itself. **Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP)** controls risky egress - copy to USB, upload to cloud, clipboard, print. No single tool is enough; you layer them.

## BitLocker: encryption at rest

**BitLocker** encrypts the entire volume with **XTS-AES** (the modern, tamper-resistant mode, default 128-bit, optionally 256-bit). The encryption key is sealed to the **Trusted Platform Module (TPM)**, a hardware chip that releases the key only if boot integrity is intact. TPM-only unlocks transparently, but adding a **PIN** (TPM+PIN) defeats pre-boot key-extraction attacks against a stolen device.

Two enrolment choices matter. **Used-space-only** encryption is fast and fine for brand-new drives; **full** encryption is mandatory for any drive that has held data, because free sectors can hold readable remnants. Critically, you must **escrow the recovery key** to Entra ID or Active Directory so a locked-out user is never stranded.

In practice you set all of this with an **Intune disk encryption policy** for fleet-wide consistency, then verify on the box:

```powershell
# Quick status and protection state
manage-bde -status C:

# List the key protectors (TPM, numerical recovery password, etc.)
manage-bde -protectors -get C:

# The PowerShell-native equivalent, richer for scripting
Get-BitLockerVolume -MountPoint C: |
  Select-Object MountPoint, VolumeStatus, EncryptionMethod,
    ProtectionStatus, EncryptionPercentage
```

## BitLocker recovery

When the TPM measurements change - a firmware update, a BIOS change, a moved disk - BitLocker enters **recovery mode** and demands the 48-digit numerical password. Because you escrowed it, you retrieve it from Entra ID or AD and unlock:

```text
manage-bde -unlock C: -RecoveryPassword 123456-...-654321
manage-bde -protectors -disable C:   # suspend during planned firmware work
```

Suspend (not decrypt) protection before TPM-affecting maintenance so the device boots without prompting, then resume.

## Purview: classification and labels

Protection at rest is not enough once a file leaves the disk. **Microsoft Purview Information Protection** classifies content using **sensitive information types (SITs)** - pattern detectors for things like card or passport numbers - and **trainable classifiers**, machine-learning models trained on examples to spot fuzzy categories such as contracts. A **sensitivity label** (for example *Confidential*) then applies persistent encryption, rights and visual marking that **travel with the file** anywhere.

## Endpoint DLP and the productivity balance

**Endpoint DLP** enforces policy at egress points on managed devices: block or audit **copy to USB, upload to cloud, clipboard paste, and print**. Combined with labels, DLP can say "a *Confidential*-labelled file may not be written to removable media". The art is balance: blunt blocking breeds shadow IT and **insider risk**. Mature rollouts start in **audit**, scope by label and group, then enforce with a **block-with-override** that captures user justification - protecting **PII** without stopping legitimate work.

## Your task

In a test tenant, create an Intune disk encryption policy that enforces XTS-AES with TPM+PIN and escrows the recovery key to Entra ID. On an enrolled device, confirm the result with `manage-bde -status` and `Get-BitLockerVolume`, then deliberately trigger recovery (change a boot setting) and recover using the escrowed key. Finally, publish one sensitivity label and build an endpoint DLP policy in audit mode that flags that label being copied to USB; review the audit events and write a one-page plan for moving it to block-with-override without disrupting a named business workflow.

slides.title: Data protection: BitLocker, DLP and Purview
slides.sub: Month 3 - Advanced Endpoint Security & Identity  |  Lesson 7
slides.narration: Welcome back. In this lesson we tackle one of the most important jobs you do as an endpoint engineer: protecting data itself. We'll cover encryption at rest with BitLocker, classification and labels with Microsoft Purview, and endpoint Data Loss Prevention, or D L P. By the end you'll be able to manage encryption from the command line and design controls that stop leaks without getting in the way of real work.

slides.title: Three states of data
bullets: At rest - sitting on a disk or drive.
In use - open on screen, in the clipboard.
In transit - over the network or onto USB.
A complete strategy covers all three.
slides.narration: Start with the mental model. Data is vulnerable in three different states. At rest, when it's just sitting on a disk. In use, when it's open on a screen or copied to the clipboard. And in transit, when it's moving across the network or being written to a U S B stick. A real data protection strategy has to cover all three. Miss one and you've left a door open.

slides.title: One control per state
bullets: BitLocker - encrypts data at rest.
Sensitivity labels - protect data in use and in transit.
Endpoint DLP - controls risky egress.
You layer them; no single tool is enough.
slides.narration: Each state has a control that fits it. BitLocker encrypts the whole volume, protecting data at rest. Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels bind protection to the file itself, so it's covered in use and in transit. And endpoint D L P controls risky egress - copy to U S B, upload to cloud, clipboard, print. The key insight: you layer these. No single tool protects everything, so we combine them deliberately.

slides.title: BitLocker fundamentals
bullets: Encrypts the volume with XTS-AES, 128 or 256-bit.
Key sealed to the TPM hardware chip.
TPM-only unlocks silently; TPM+PIN adds a secret.
TPM+PIN defeats pre-boot key-extraction attacks.
slides.narration: Let's get into BitLocker. It encrypts the entire volume using X T S - A E S, the modern tamper-resistant mode, either 128 or 256-bit. The encryption key is sealed to the Trusted Platform Module, the T P M, a hardware chip that only releases the key if the boot process is intact. T P M-only unlocks silently, which is convenient. But adding a P I N - that's T P M plus P I N - means a thief with a stolen laptop can't extract the key at the pre-boot stage. For high-risk devices, the P I N is worth it.

slides.title: Encryption scope and escrow
bullets: Used-space-only: fast, only for brand-new drives.
Full encryption: required for any drive that held data.
Free sectors can hold readable remnants.
Always escrow the recovery key to Entra ID or AD.
slides.narration: Two choices matter when you turn BitLocker on. Used-space-only encryption is quick and perfectly fine for a brand-new drive. But for any drive that has already held data, you must use full encryption, because blocks marked free can still contain readable remnants of old files. And whatever you choose, always escrow the recovery key - to Entra I D or Active Directory - so a locked-out user is never stranded with no way back in.

slides.title: Manage and audit from the CLI
bullets: manage-bde -status shows percent, method, protection.
manage-bde -protectors -get lists the key protectors.
Get-BitLockerVolume is the scripting-friendly cmdlet.
Set the policy fleet-wide via Intune, verify on the box.
slides.code:
manage-bde -status C:
manage-bde -protectors -get C:

Get-BitLockerVolume -MountPoint C: |
  Select-Object MountPoint, VolumeStatus,
    EncryptionMethod, ProtectionStatus,
    EncryptionPercentage
slides.narration: You'll configure BitLocker across the fleet with an Intune disk encryption policy, but you verify it on the device. Manage dash b d e dash status shows the percentage encrypted, the method, and whether protection is on. Manage dash b d e dash protectors dash get lists the protectors - the T P M, the numerical recovery password, and so on. And Get dash BitLocker Volume is the PowerShell-native cmdlet, which is far nicer when you're scripting reports across many machines. Learn all three; you'll use them constantly.

slides.title: BitLocker recovery
bullets: Boot changes trip recovery mode - firmware, BIOS, moved disk.
It demands the 48-digit recovery password.
Retrieve the key from Entra ID or AD, then unlock.
Suspend protection before planned firmware work.
slides.narration: Sometimes BitLocker drops into recovery mode - after a firmware update, a BIOS change, or a disk moved to new hardware - and asks for the 48-digit numerical password. Because you escrowed it, you simply look it up in Entra I D or A D and unlock the drive. The pro move: before any planned maintenance that touches the T P M or firmware, suspend protection rather than decrypt. The device then boots without prompting, and you resume protection afterwards. Suspend, don't decrypt - decrypting a whole drive wastes hours.

slides.title: Purview: classify and label
bullets: Sensitive info types detect patterns like card numbers.
Trainable classifiers learn fuzzy categories from examples.
Sensitivity labels apply encryption, rights and marking.
Protection travels with the file, anywhere it goes.
slides.narration: BitLocker protects data on the disk, but the moment a file leaves that disk the encryption no longer applies. That's where Microsoft Purview comes in. It classifies content using sensitive information types - pattern detectors for things like card or passport numbers - and trainable classifiers, which are machine-learning models you train on examples to recognise fuzzier things like contracts. You then apply a sensitivity label, say Confidential, which bakes encryption, rights and visual marking right into the file. That protection travels with the document wherever it goes, even off the managed device.

slides.title: Endpoint DLP and balance
bullets: Blocks or audits copy to USB, cloud, clipboard, print.
Combine with labels: Confidential files can't hit USB.
Blunt blocking breeds shadow IT and insider risk.
Start in audit, scope by label and group, then block-with-override.
slides.narration: Endpoint D L P enforces policy at the egress points on managed devices - copy to U S B, upload to cloud, clipboard paste, and print. Combined with labels you can say a Confidential file may never be written to removable media. But here's the judgement call: if you just block everything bluntly, people route around you, and that shadow I T is itself an insider-risk problem. So mature teams start in audit mode, scope tightly by label and group, then enforce with a block-with-override that captures the user's business justification. You protect the P I I without stopping legitimate work.

slides.title: Recap & your task
bullets: Cover all three states: at rest, in use, in transit.
BitLocker plus labels plus endpoint DLP, layered.
Always escrow recovery keys; suspend before firmware work.
Task: enforce, recover, label, and pilot a DLP policy in audit.
slides.narration: Let's recap. Protect data in all three states - at rest, in use, in transit - by layering BitLocker, Purview sensitivity labels, and endpoint D L P. Always escrow your recovery keys, and suspend protection rather than decrypt before firmware work. Your task: in a test tenant, build an Intune policy enforcing X T S - A E S with T P M plus P I N and key escrow to Entra I D. Verify it with manage dash b d e dash status and Get dash BitLocker Volume, then deliberately trigger recovery and recover using the escrowed key. Finally, publish a sensitivity label, build an endpoint D L P policy in audit mode that flags that label copied to U S B, and write a one-page plan to move it to block-with-override without disrupting a named workflow. See you in the next lesson.
